KnightLoader 2.9.8 brings the Android app level with the web interface, and the browser extension pairs on a relay of your own.

## ✨ Added

- **The browser extension pairs on your own relay.** A Relay field under the phrase takes the address your instances use, https:// or wss://. Left empty, it is the project relay. Thanks to @MueChris82 ([#329](https://github.com/junkerderprovinz/knightloader/issues/329)).
- **The Android app has the same Relay field.** Scanning the QR code fills it, and typed words pair on it as well.
- **Act on links and packages from the app.** The More menu on each row pauses, resumes, retries, rechecks, starts at once, moves to the top or bottom, sets the priority and removes, and a removal can be undone. One button resets every failed download.
- **Properties in the app.** Rename a link or a package, move links to another package, and set the category, folder, archive and link passwords, comment and connections.
- **Add links with options.** Package, folder, category, priority, unpacking, comment and passwords, as on the web.
- **Containers and .torrent files from the phone.** Choose a file on the add screen takes DLC, CCF, RSDF, NZB and text files of links, and shows a torrent's files to pick from first.
- **Search, quick filters and saved views in the app.** Saved views are shared with the web interface, and the Collector lists rejected links and links that were not added.
- **Speed limit and parallel downloads from the app,** in a quick settings window on the queue card.
- **Save a finished file to the phone,** every file of a torrent included, through Android's own folder picker.
- **Pick a video's format and quality when adding it,** audio conversions included.
- **More notifications.** The app tells you when unpacking finishes or fails, and when an account is paused or back in use.
- **The phone reaches all of this through narrow routes of its own.** The settings stay closed to it.

## 🐛 Fixed

- **The browser extension works with an instance that serves the relay.** Its handshake carries the extension's own origin, which the instance turned away with 403 before the relay saw it. Extension origins now pass on /relay/connect and nowhere else. Thanks to @MueChris82 for the careful handshake tests ([#329](https://github.com/junkerderprovinz/knightloader/issues/329)).
- **Calls reach an instance while it reconnects.** Right after a rename, the relay could report the reconnecting instance offline to the others, and a call that changes something, such as sending links, failed while the instance's address briefly refused the connection. KnightLoader takes ParleyPort 1.3.8, which keeps the relay's messages in order and tries such a call again.
- **The app connects again when the relay drops it silently.** A call that goes unanswered now makes the app drop the dead connection and dial again, instead of staying at "connecting".
- **The app says why an instance turns it away.** The downloads screen shows the instance's reason under "connecting", for example that the phone still waits for approval.
- **An approved phone gets everything at once.** Saved views, the finished and torrent cards and the instance's look are read again once a phone that waited for approval gets through.
- **Pressing Add twice saves an instance once.**
- **Rejected links no longer show up as collected links in the app.**
- **Every screen of the app stays above Android's navigation bar.** With three-button navigation the bar covered the foot of a screen, such as the button that adds an instance.
- **The add screen scrolls** once a torrent's files or a video's choices open, so the button that adds stays in reach.
- **A long button label wraps and is hyphenated** instead of ending in an ellipsis.
- **The app's Firefox button opens the add-on's listing** instead of saying Soon.

## 🌐 Translations

- **Every new text in the app and the extension speaks all 42 languages.** Most come from the web interface's own translations, so the app and the web say the same thing.
